title: Hide empty sensor categories
line: The System Monitor sensor picker no longer shows categories that have no sensors, like Power on a computer without a battery.
explanation: The ksystemstats daemon's allSensors() reply included an entry for every sensor container (category) and object, even when they held no sensors. The sensor tree model in libksysguard turns each entry into a tree item, so an empty container such as Power on a machine without a battery showed up as a category with nothing inside, and could even be picked as if it were a sensor. The daemon now only lists a container or object when it contains at least one sensor, which hides every empty category, as asked in comment 1.

commits.message:
daemon: don't list containers and objects without sensors

allSensors() listed every container and object even when they had no
sensors, so the sensor picker showed empty categories such as Power on a
computer without a battery. Only list them when they contain a sensor.

BUG: 440662

media.caption: Widget settings, Sensors Details picker with no battery: Power is listed with no arrow and nothing inside
Same picker with the patched ksystemstats: Power is gone, the other categories are unchanged

reviews.text: Filtering empty objects and containers in ksystemstats's Daemon::allSensors() fixes the root cause in the right layer so all clients (widgets and System Monitor) hide empty categories like Power on battery-less machines. The logic handles containers with multiple objects cleanly without changing output when sensors are present, and the screenshots and regression counts verify the behavior.

Leaving empty containers and objects out of allSensors() does hide Power at startup, and the screenshots and allSensors diff support that. But it is a regression in the exact case the bug is about. The power plugin adds a Solid battery object at runtime for any battery that appears (Bluetooth mice, keyboards, headsets), and the daemon then only sends sensorAdded for the sensor paths. SensorTreeModel builds the missing Power branch with segmentNameForRegEx(), which falls back to the raw id, so a desktop user who connects a peripheral later sees a lowercase 'power' category for the rest of the session. Today the container keeps its translated name. The notes treat this as a narrow edge case, but on desktops it is common, so the fix should not drop the container and object names the client needs.
changes: Keep the container/object names available to clients: either keep listing them in allSensors() and hide branches without sensor leaves in libksysguard's SensorTreeModel (store non-sensor entries only as names, create tree items only for real sensor paths), or make the daemon publish names for containers/objects that get their first sensor at runtime

Verify the runtime case: start with no battery, add one (e.g. a fake UPower/Solid battery or peripheral) while the picker's model is alive, and show the category appears as 'Power' with a proper object name
